Abase

uh-BASE · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To abase to lower in rank, dignity, or self-respect.

The general refused to abase himself before the invading commander, even facing execution.

Worked Example

Desperate for the loan, the merchant abased himself, kneeling and begging the moneylender for mercy in front of the whole marketplace.

Abase describes a deliberate lowering of one's own dignity -- here, publicly kneeling and begging -- not simply feeling embarrassed.

How Abase Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

degrade

degrade: lower someone's dignity or status

humble

humble: make someone feel less important, often less harshly

Antonyms

exalt

exalt: raise to a higher rank or status

dignify

dignify: give a sense of honor or importance to

How Strong Is It? — humble → abase → debase

humble vs. abase

humble vs. abase: To humble someone is a general softening of their pride; to abase them is a deeper, deliberate lowering of their dignity or status.

debase vs. abase

debase vs. abase: Debase pushes further than abase, often implying a lasting, corrupting loss of value or worth, not just a momentary act of humiliation.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — a-

prefix — a-: to, toward (intensifying) (Old French)

root — bas

root — bas: low (Latin (bassus))

suffix — -e

suffix — -e: verb-forming ending (English)

Put it together

Put it together: a- ('to') + bas ('low') + -e together literally mean 'to make low' -- exactly what abase does to someone's dignity.

Use the root in a new word: debase

Use the root in a new word: debase: Debase uses the same Latin root (bassus, 'low') with a different prefix, meaning to lower the quality or value of something.

Word Choice

Abase is formal and literary -- often used reflexively ('abase oneself') and almost always about dignity, not physical position.
